author: /root
rationale: Each context binds independently replayed C and Ada events reports and named C/AUnit evidence. Exact source paths, predicates, dynamic callback invocations and configurations come from the hash-bound execution packet.

Default userdata omission resolves through six instrumented assertions. The silent weak-delegation loop runs in both configurations. Each instrumented Ada parent records actual allocation refusal and the instrumented C reference uses its real test allocator.
Ordinary and instrumented runs verify the immutable source and separately hashed return wrapper, matching children and probe identities, exact output, shutdown and balanced memory.
API decisions use the complete 77-entry reviewed case mapping. All 41 C case witnesses, 35 AUnit labels, Ada image identities and reference GC/IO contract captures were replayed in each context.
final_acceptance_pending: Final-revision operation runs and independently approved final matrix.

decisions.basis: environment-and-metatable-protection. All 19 semantic sections, helper invocations, both T guards, stream dependency, terminal OK and return 12 require independent execution evidence. Whole-file semantic audit expands into all actual assertions and the silent guarded refusal block.

Callbacks receive owned argument windows and captured cells, protected errors retain exact values, nested callbacks recover, and non-yieldable calls return synchronously without invoking their supplied continuation. Only the synchronous/non-yieldable API paths directly exercised by this batch are candidates. Yieldable C continuations, C coroutine resumption and the remaining full ABI stay pending. Foreign jumps must never cross active Ada frames.

Actual callback/data identity, seeded construction, refusal at measured growth positions, usable recovery, and physical release of all allocator-owned blocks. AUnit and the public GC contract additionally exercise state-close finalizers. This group does not establish arbitrary foreign allocator replacement compatibility or unrelated allocator parity.

Indices resolve before mutation, callbacks see their argument window, results are adjusted including multiple results, and failed growth preserves the live prefix and later calls. Macros must be checked through the pinned headers and their expanded public calls. Merely compiling the macro name does not establish its observable stack effect.

Success, nil, absent optional arguments and actual full userdata remain distinct through public type queries and callback results. The T.newuserdata optional-argument checks in tests/c/conformance_adapter.c also exercise lua_isnoneornil. Review invalid/missing arguments independently of successful allocations. The production adapter userdata driver uses this macro for optional argument defaults. Explicit-argument AUnit Userdata alone cannot certify absent/nil defaults; upstream userdata calls and their actual configurations must supply that evidence.

Embedded NUL and high bytes retain exact lengths and stable rooted addresses; null string input becomes nil, and real allocation failure stays within the C-owned error boundary. Warning fragments and adapter diagnostics exercise actual retained byte strings. Source citations must not substitute for refusal/recovery execution.

The public payload contains the actual FILE pointer and callable closer; reopening io retains live stream metatable identity; os returns callable exports without implicit global publication; native closer invocation closes the owned stream. The standalone IO contract compares C and Ada with zero outstanding allocator storage after close. Native device/date/shell equivalents and partial-write behavior need their own source-bound review; these layout cases do not establish all IO semantics.
